    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401486/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There is a Flash game, <em>Castlevania: The Blood Way</em>, which is hard to find on the internet today. One problem with that game is that it uses external resources: it loads SWFs from a specific domain, including level SWFs (0 to around 11 levels).</p>
<p>I've the SWF: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link</a></p>
<p>But the game doesn't play anymore. I tested it in the Ruffle player a few months ago and it worked, but the game stopped working now. I believe that the external resources have expired. Note that it doesn't work in the Flash Player projector too anymore.</p>
<p>I used FFDec a few months ago and was able to manipulate these external resources, but I lost everything. For some reason, now that I go to FFDec, I don't have idea of what are the domains. For example, I see that FFDec shows this ActionScript 2 code:</p>
<pre><code>loadMovieNum("musics/introB.swf",1,"GET");
</code></pre>
<p>The problem is, which is the base path for this resource? I tried to search for, say, <code>musics/introB.swf</code> in archive.org and didn't find anything. Not sure if this kind of search works in archive.org though. Any idea of what I'm missing? Because I was able to see the full absolute path of the resources...</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>There is a Flash game, <em>Castlevania: The Blood Way</em>, which is hard to find on the internet today. One problem with that game is that it uses external resources: it loads SWFs from a specific domain, including level SWFs (0 to around 11 levels).</p>
<p>I've the SWF: <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YE-S8ynq_mscVC5dblHneWbCZ6o3-E8g/view?usp=share_link</a></p>
<p>But the game doesn't play anymore. I tested it in the Ruffle player a few months ago and it worked, but the game stopped working now. I believe that the external resources have expired. Note that it doesn't work in the Flash Player projector too anymore.</p>
<p>I used FFDec a few months ago and was able to manipulate these external resources, but I lost everything. For some reason, now that I go to FFDec, I don't have idea of what are the domains. For example, I see that FFDec shows this ActionScript 2 code:</p>
<pre><code>loadMovieNum("musics/introB.swf",1,"GET");
</code></pre>
<p>The problem is, which is the base path for this resource? I tried to search for, say, <code>musics/introB.swf</code> in archive.org and didn't find anything. Not sure if this kind of search works in archive.org though. Any idea of what I'm missing? Because I was able to see the full absolute path of the resources...</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The idea behind my contraption is to trap players in lava by deactivating an area of fence gates under some carpet. This pushes the players upwards into the lava and there items fall onto the carpet. (Basically killing a player with lava without burning their items.)</p>
<p>My problem is that I'm not sure how to toggle the full area of fence gates from the underneath.</p>
<p>(Where the grass is below the fence gates.)
<a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Image for context:" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The solutions I thought of are:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>I can try and toggle a bunch of redstone torches underneath (due to them activating upwards), but then how do I activate the torches?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Observers also activate upwards, but for only a tick, how can I make it on/off like the torches?</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>If you have any ideas on how to fix my issue, please share them here. If you have any redesigns for a more improvised trap, please put them here as well. (No commands/No mods) Thank you!</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401509/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>While I wrote my last comment, I had an idea that's at least not overly terrible. It works with arbitrarily large planes, is "just" 6 blocks tall and at most 3 blocks longer in one direction and 1 in another than the area you want to toggle. That's already way better than anything else I could think of.</p>
<p><img alt="sticky blocks pushing up redstone blocks" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0mx3o.png"/></p>
<p>The idea was to use slime/honey blocks to increase the amount of redstone blocks you can move towards the fence gates at once, basically shrinking the problem of how many blocks need to be powered at once. Theoretically you could use 6 slime/honey blocks and 6 redstone blocks each, but due to the eternally annoying bug <a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-108" rel="nofollow noreferrer">MC-108</a>, this doesn't work. The redstone blocks need to be even further away from the pistons, so you can only use 5 redstone blocks per piston.</p>
<p>You could use a similar method to power up to 11 pistons at a time with redstone blocks, but then the circuit would grow even further downwards.<br/>
You can make the rows of redstone and repeaters longer between the parts where the signal snakes around, to use the full power level 15, and you can infinitely tile this pattern, alternating between slime and honey blocks wherever they touch.<br/>
There's probably a way to make the redstone/repeater part a bit more compact, but it's probably usually not worth it.</p>
<p>This all looks really messy, but it might be the easiest way. A similar problem are 1×1 lamp screens where every pixel can be controlled individually, which experts have worked on for years. Those contraptions can get extremely complicated.<br/>
In general, whenever you can avoid this problem, do that instead.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The idea behind my contraption is to trap players in lava by deactivating an area of fence gates under some carpet. This pushes the players upwards into the lava and there items fall onto the carpet. (Basically killing a player with lava without burning their items.)</p>
<p>My problem is that I'm not sure how to toggle the full area of fence gates from the underneath.</p>
<p>(Where the grass is below the fence gates.)
<a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Image for context:" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The solutions I thought of are:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>I can try and toggle a bunch of redstone torches underneath (due to them activating upwards), but then how do I activate the torches?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Observers also activate upwards, but for only a tick, how can I make it on/off like the torches?</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>If you have any ideas on how to fix my issue, please share them here. If you have any redesigns for a more improvised trap, please put them here as well. (No commands/No mods) Thank you!</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>While I wrote my last comment, I had an idea that's at least not overly terrible. It works with arbitrarily large planes, is "just" 6 blocks tall and at most 3 blocks longer in one direction and 1 in another than the area you want to toggle. That's already way better than anything else I could think of.</p>
<p><img alt="sticky blocks pushing up redstone blocks" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0mx3o.png"/></p>
<p>The idea was to use slime/honey blocks to increase the amount of redstone blocks you can move towards the fence gates at once, basically shrinking the problem of how many blocks need to be powered at once. Theoretically you could use 6 slime/honey blocks and 6 redstone blocks each, but due to the eternally annoying bug <a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-108" rel="nofollow noreferrer">MC-108</a>, this doesn't work. The redstone blocks need to be even further away from the pistons, so you can only use 5 redstone blocks per piston.</p>
<p>You could use a similar method to power up to 11 pistons at a time with redstone blocks, but then the circuit would grow even further downwards.<br/>
You can make the rows of redstone and repeaters longer between the parts where the signal snakes around, to use the full power level 15, and you can infinitely tile this pattern, alternating between slime and honey blocks wherever they touch.<br/>
There's probably a way to make the redstone/repeater part a bit more compact, but it's probably usually not worth it.</p>
<p>This all looks really messy, but it might be the easiest way. A similar problem are 1×1 lamp screens where every pixel can be controlled individually, which experts have worked on for years. Those contraptions can get extremely complicated.<br/>
In general, whenever you can avoid this problem, do that instead.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The idea behind my contraption is to trap players in lava by deactivating an area of fence gates under some carpet. This pushes the players upwards into the lava and there items fall onto the carpet. (Basically killing a player with lava without burning their items.)</p>
<p>My problem is that I'm not sure how to toggle the full area of fence gates from the underneath.</p>
<p>(Where the grass is below the fence gates.)
<a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="Image for context:" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/iWjNs.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The solutions I thought of are:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>I can try and toggle a bunch of redstone torches underneath (due to them activating upwards), but then how do I activate the torches?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Observers also activate upwards, but for only a tick, how can I make it on/off like the torches?</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>If you have any ideas on how to fix my issue, please share them here. If you have any redesigns for a more improvised trap, please put them here as well. (No commands/No mods) Thank you!</p>
</div>

<div class="answer js-answer accepted-answer js-accepted-answer" data-answerid="401509" data-highest-scored="1" data-parentid="401497" data-position-on-page="1" data-question-has-accepted-highest-score="1" data-score="4" id="answer-401509" itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemscope="" itemtype="https://schema.org/Answer">

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401509/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>While I wrote my last comment, I had an idea that's at least not overly terrible. It works with arbitrarily large planes, is "just" 6 blocks tall and at most 3 blocks longer in one direction and 1 in another than the area you want to toggle. That's already way better than anything else I could think of.</p>
<p><img alt="sticky blocks pushing up redstone blocks" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0mx3o.png"/></p>
<p>The idea was to use slime/honey blocks to increase the amount of redstone blocks you can move towards the fence gates at once, basically shrinking the problem of how many blocks need to be powered at once. Theoretically you could use 6 slime/honey blocks and 6 redstone blocks each, but due to the eternally annoying bug <a href="https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-108" rel="nofollow noreferrer">MC-108</a>, this doesn't work. The redstone blocks need to be even further away from the pistons, so you can only use 5 redstone blocks per piston.</p>
<p>You could use a similar method to power up to 11 pistons at a time with redstone blocks, but then the circuit would grow even further downwards.<br/>
You can make the rows of redstone and repeaters longer between the parts where the signal snakes around, to use the full power level 15, and you can infinitely tile this pattern, alternating between slime and honey blocks wherever they touch.<br/>
There's probably a way to make the redstone/repeater part a bit more compact, but it's probably usually not worth it.</p>
<p>This all looks really messy, but it might be the easiest way. A similar problem are 1×1 lamp screens where every pixel can be controlled individually, which experts have worked on for years. Those contraptions can get extremely complicated.<br/>
In general, whenever you can avoid this problem, do that instead.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<svg aria-hidden="true" class="fc-theme-primary-500 js-saves-btn-selected d-none svg-icon iconBookmark" height="18" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18"><path d="M3 17V3c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14l-6-4-6 4Z"></path></svg>
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="js-saves-btn-unselected svg-icon iconBookmarkAlt" height="18" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18"><path d="m9 10.6 4 2.66V3H5v10.26l4-2.66ZM3 17V3c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14l-6-4-6 4Z"></path></svg>

<div class="ta-center">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="svg-icon iconCheckmarkLg" height="36" viewbox="0 0 36 36" width="36"><path d="m6 14 8 8L30 6v8L14 30l-8-8v-8Z"></path></svg>

</div>
<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401551/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<svg aria-hidden="true" class="js-saves-btn-unselected svg-icon iconBookmarkAlt" height="18" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18"><path d="m9 10.6 4 2.66V3H5v10.26l4-2.66ZM3 17V3c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v14l-6-4-6 4Z"></path></svg>

<div class="ta-center">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="svg-icon iconCheckmarkLg" height="36" viewbox="0 0 36 36" width="36"><path d="m6 14 8 8L30 6v8L14 30l-8-8v-8Z"></path></svg>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401551/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I have two 1.19 Minecraft java servers running on an Ubuntu machine. From in game, how would I send a player from server A, to server B? It needs to be something that both a command block could run, and also a player.</p>
<p>I've searched around, but all I can find is either for Bedrock, or involves extensive plugins. Is there a way to do this in vanilla? If not, then I don't mind using plugins/mods as long as it's not overly complicated. I'd also like to be able to execute the command via a python script.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>No, you can't do this in Vanilla. Separate servers are separate. From all I've heard about these mods, they're all pretty complicated, because you need to trick a client into doing this, which isn't normally made to support it. And both servers needs to know what is going on and some program needs to handle the transition between them.</p>
<p>I would recommend just telling people to switch servers or to to try to implement everything with one server, whatever you're trying to do. Maybe asking how to do that would be a better question (meaning: one that gives you a more helpful answer).</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As others have pointed out, you cannot do this with just vanilla servers.</p>
<p>The probably best known solution to do this is a <a href="https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/bungeecord/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Bungeecord</a> setup. Bungeecord is <strong>not a minecraft server</strong>, but acts as a sort of reverse proxy for your players. They will connect to the bungee server, which will then forward them to the respective running server. There are some alternatives like <a href="https://github.com/PaperMC/Waterfall" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Waterfall from the PaperMC project</a>.</p>
<p>Afaik this setup requires you to use spigot/bukkit/paper servers, but there again are options to add plugins to this and make it compatible with vanilla. A quick search points to <a href="https://github.com/Thinkofname/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Vanillacord</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ME1312/VanillaCord/tree/master/src/main/java/uk/co/thinkofdeath/vanillacord" rel="nofollow noreferrer">its updates</a>.</p>
</div>

            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<p>I wanna know how to kill specific  modded items if the item has a color code name, like in this case it's called Katana Kuzanagi (the kuzangi part is red).<br/>
I tried doing §4 to make it red but that doesn't work.</p>
<p>The command I'm using is</p>
<pre><code>/kill @e[type=item,name="Katana Kuzanagi"]
</code></pre>

            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I wanna know how to kill specific  modded items if the item has a color code name, like in this case it's called Katana Kuzanagi (the kuzangi part is red).<br/>
I tried doing §4 to make it red but that doesn't work.</p>
<p>The command I'm using is</p>
<pre><code>/kill @e[type=item,name="Katana Kuzanagi"]
</code></pre>

            location = 1;

            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way.

            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();

        });

<p>I wanna know how to kill specific  modded items if the item has a color code name, like in this case it's called Katana Kuzanagi (the kuzangi part is red).<br/>
I tried doing §4 to make it red but that doesn't work.</p>
<p>The command I'm using is</p>
<pre><code>/kill @e[type=item,name="Katana Kuzanagi"]
</code></pre>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I would do one of the following:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>Get a new account (Hopefully you won't need to)</p>
</li>
<li><p>Contact support <a href="https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new" rel="nofollow noreferrer">https://help.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/requests/new</a></p>
<p>When contacting support, try to get proof of owning the account.</p>
</li>
<li><p>Try to reset the password via email. However, if this is an older account that hasn't migrated then this may not be possible.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Good luck!</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>If I ever lose internet access and then get it back, when I open Halo Infinite it has the "No internet" error at the top right of the screen.  When I open the multiplayer tab it searches for a bit and then gives me an error saying it can't connect, even though I do have internet.  Apparently Halo is too stupid to recognize when my internet works.  I have tried closing it through the task manager, closing every Xbox related app on the task manager, signing out of steam, restarting the game and it still doesn't work.  I am trying to sign out of the Xbox app but whenever this happens it wont let me!  The sign out button is greyed out.  The only thing that works is restarting my pc which I would rather not do every time I temporarily lose internet.  How do I fix this issue?</p>
</div>
